nodes.label: GSM-Symbolic: Understanding the Limitations of Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
nodes.author: Iman Mirzadeh, Keivan Alizadeh, Hooman Shahrokhi, Oncel Tuzel, Samy Bengio, Mehrdad Farajtabar
nodes.rationale: Published at ICLR 2025. Introduces GSM-Symbolic benchmark to evaluate mathematical reasoning in LLMs through symbolic templates, revealing fragility and pattern-matching behavior rather than genuine logical reasoning.

nodes.label: GSM-Symbolic Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Symbolic template-based benchmark enabling generation of diverse question variants from GSM8K, allowing controllable evaluation of LLM mathematical reasoning across different instantiations and difficulty levels.

nodes.label: GSM-NoOp Dataset
nodes.rationale: Dataset variant adding seemingly relevant but ultimately inconsequential statements to questions, designed to test whether LLMs can discern relevant information for problem-solving.

nodes.label: LLM Mathematical Reasoning Limitations
nodes.rationale: Core finding: LLMs exhibit high performance variance across question instantiations, sensitivity to numerical changes, degradation with increased complexity, and catastrophic drops with irrelevant information—indicating pattern-matching rather than formal reasoning.

nodes.label: Pattern-Matching Hypothesis for LLMs
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that LLMs perform probabilistic pattern-matching rather than formal logical reasoning, explaining sensitivity to input variations and inability to handle out-of-distribution information.

nodes.label: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Prompting
nodes.rationale: Prompting technique enabling LLMs to show intermediate reasoning steps; used in GSM-Symbolic evaluation with 8-shot examples.

nodes.label: Data Contamination in GSM8K
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis that GSM8K test examples may have inadvertently entered LLM training sets, explaining why original GSM8K performance often exceeds GSM-Symbolic distribution mean.

nodes.label: Length Generalization
nodes.rationale: Ability to apply known logical steps on larger inputs; key aspect of genuine reasoning distinct from pattern-matching.

nodes.label: Chinese Room Argument
nodes.rationale: Philosophical argument distinguishing true comprehension from symbol manipulation; referenced to support distinction between genuine reasoning and pattern-matching in LLMs.

nodes.label: Token Bias in LLMs
nodes.rationale: Phenomenon where LLM outputs change drastically with single token input changes, indicating strong sensitivity and fragility in reasoning.

nodes.label: Exponential Probability Decay with Token Count
nodes.rationale: Finding that probability of correct multi-token output decreases exponentially with number of tokens, indicating inherent unreliability in complex reasoning.
